channel.title: GetUp - In-Depth Java Engineering Writing
channel.description: Long-form Java engineering writing from real implementation work: chess engine internals, move generation, search algorithms, and JVM exception debugging.

item.title: Bitboards Explained: Representing a Chess Board in 64 Bits
item.description: A chess board has 64 squares; a Java long has 64 bits. The explanation I wish I'd had — why engines switch from arrays to bitboards, the bitwise tricks, move generation, and the bugs that taught me how they really work.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: Generating Sliding Piece Moves Without Magic Bitboards (And Why I Started There)
item.description: Every resource jumped straight to magic bitboards. I skipped them and wrote the plain ray-walking generator instead — the direction arrays, the blocker logic, the bugs that ate two weekends, and why correctness beats clever optimisation.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: Magic Bitboards in Java: What Finally Made Them Click
item.description: I closed the tab the first time I read about magic bitboards. Months later the same page made sense. The intuition behind occupancy masks and blockers, concise Java code, and every bug that cost me an evening.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: Perft Testing: How I Found 4 Move-Generation Bugs in One Afternoon
item.description: My engine played legal-looking chess, and legal-looking is not legal. Perft gave me a number that was either right or wrong, and perft divide told me exactly where the en passant, castling, promotion and file-wrapping bugs were hiding.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: Handling En Passant, Castling Rights, and the 50-Move Rule Correctly
item.description: Three rules every tutorial hand-waves. They are not hard to understand, they are hard to get right, because none of them live on the board. A stale en passant square, rights that outlived a captured rook, and a clock counting the wrong thing.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: Minimax to Alpha-Beta: Measuring the Actual Node Reduction
item.description: A correct move generator still plays random chess. So I wrote minimax, added alpha-beta, and counted every node instead of trusting the textbook square root. Move ordering turned out to do almost nothing from the start position and almost everything in a real midgame.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: Why I Built a Chess Engine in Java Instead of Another CRUD App
item.description: After a stack of Todo apps and inventory systems, I built a chess engine in Java. The design decisions, the minimax and alpha-beta code, the brutal bugs, and what a genuinely hard project actually teaches you.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: Writing a Chess Evaluation Function: Material, Piece-Square Tables, Mobility
item.description: A correct search that only counts material shuffles rooks, refuses to castle and parks knights on the rim. Piece values, 64 numbers per piece type, a midgame-to-endgame taper, a mobility term, and the symmetry test that caught three bugs in one assertion.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: Implementing the UCI Protocol in Plain Java (No Frameworks)
item.description: Move generation, search and evaluation all worked, and Arena still showed the engine as not responding. The handshake, the position and go parsers, the worker thread that keeps stop readable, and the missing flush that lost a game on time.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: Deploying a Lichess Bot: BOT Account, API Streaming, and What Broke
item.description: The engine played fine offline, then sat still in its first live game while the clock ran out. The irreversible BOT upgrade, two NDJSON streams, a systemd unit, and eight failures that only appear against real opponents.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: ConcurrentModificationException: Why Your For-Loop Breaks and Four Ways to Fix It
item.description: It has nothing to do with threads, and removing the second-to-last element does not throw at all - it silently skips the last one. The modCount machinery, three real causes, and four fixes with their actual costs.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: NullPointerException in Java 21: Reading the Helpful Message
item.description: JEP 358 turned the emptiest stack trace in Java into a sentence. The grammar of that sentence, three production causes with the exact message each one throws, and the places it still leaves you stranded.
item.dc:creator: Vijay

item.title: ClassNotFoundException vs NoClassDefFoundError: The Difference Actually Matters
item.description: One is a checked exception you asked for, the other is an Error the JVM hands you — and "Could not initialize class" does not mean the class is missing at all. The three loading phases, three real causes, and the fixes with their costs.
item.dc:creator: Vijay
